name: Bahasa Melayu Jambi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Husin, Nurzuir, Zailoet, M. Atar Semi, Isma Nasrul Karim, Desmawati Radjab & Djurip. 1985. Struktur bahasa Melayu Jambi. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. Secondary confirmation: Anderbeck, Karl Ronald. 2008. Malay dialects of the Batanghari River Basin (Jambi, Sumatra). SIL e-Books 6. Dallas: SIL International, p. 28.
catalog_locator: Husin et al. 1985, sect. 2.4 'Tekanan', pp. 32-33. Anderbeck 2008, sect. 3.2.1, p. 28 and fn. 22.
catalog_quote: 2.4 Tekanan. Tekanan dalam bahasa Melayu Jambi dibagi atas tekanan kata dan tekanan kalimat. Tekanan kata tidak membedakan arti dan biasanya jatuh pada suku kata akhir. [p. 33] Contoh: /rumah/ 'rumah', /ŋopi/ 'mengopi', /terbaka/ 'terbakar', /menjauh/ 'menjauh', /membacoka/ 'membacakan', /meñulamkan/ 'menyulamkan'. Tekanan kalimat pada umumnya jatuh pada akhir suku kata pada kata terakhir dalam kalimat itu. Contoh: /maʔ tu tukaŋ cuci/ 'Ibu itu tukang cuci', /uraŋ nan kuat tu petani/ 'Orang yang kuat itu petani'. Tekanan kalimat juga jatuh pada kata yang dipentingkan. [Translation: Stress in Jambi Malay is divided into word stress and sentence stress. Word stress does not distinguish meaning and usually falls on the final syllable. Examples: /rumah/ 'house', /ŋopi/ 'to drink coffee', /terbaka/ 'burnt', /menjauh/ 'to move away', /membacoka/ 'to read (for someone)', /meñulamkan/ 'to embroider (for someone)'. Sentence stress generally falls on the final syllable of the last word in the sentence. ... Sentence stress also falls on the word that is emphasised.] -- Anderbeck 2008: 28: 'Stress regularly falls on the ultimate syllable.' fn. 22: 'This is true in elicitation mode. Tadmor (p.c.) has suggested that JM accent might more correctly be described as utterance final.'
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and normally falls on the last syllable of the word (examples per the same page as rendered by Wikipedia: /rumah/, /ŋopi/, /terbaka/, /mend͡ʒauh/, /mebat͡ʃoka/, /meɲulamkan/, i.e. final even in affixed words); sentence stress falls on the final syllable of the last word of the sentence.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the passage seen.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'biasanya' (usually); no explicit exceptions in the passage seen.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('tekanan kata') stated separately from sentence-level ('tekanan kalimat'); examples are citation forms including derived words. Describes the Jambi-city (lowland) variety.
new_statements.identity_note: Husin et al. 1985 describe the lowland Jambi Malay of Jambi city and environs (the trill-[r] variety 'spoken around Jambi city', per Krulikowska et al. 2020: 174 citing Husin 1985: 12-13), i.e. jamb1236 proper. Yanti/Cole/Hermon describe the Jambi Seberang (Kota Jambi) and Mudung Darat dialects; Krulikowska et al. 2020 describe the upstream Sarolangun variety; all fall under jamb1236.
